findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never migrated to the Clients schema
findings.body: `init` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore retain only the old Users resources/scopes and never receive the `Clients` resource, `configure`, or the new role-mapping scopes. Creating a client permission in such a realm will fail scope/resource resolution (and all-clients permissions have no resource to attach to), so the newly added feature only works in newly initialized realms. The initialization path needs to reconcile/add missing schema scopes and resource-type resources for an existing admin-permissions client.

findings.title: MANAGE_CLIENTS administrators lose client role-mapping access under V2
findings.body: All three role-mapping checks (`canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles`) evaluate only a V2 authorization permission. Unlike the legacy evaluator, they do not grant access to callers holding the built-in `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin role. Consequently, an ordinary realm administrator with `manage-clients` can manage a client but receives Forbidden responses when assigning that client's roles or managing composites unless an additional V2 policy is created. Preserve the built-in-role short-circuit in these methods.

findings.title: V2 client resources are left orphaned when a client is removed
findings.body: The removal listener is now gated on the legacy `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature rather than the V2 feature. When only `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled, removing a client no longer invokes the cleanup path at all. This PR creates per-client authorization resources and policies, so deleting clients accumulates orphaned resources/policies in the admin-permissions resource server. The V2 implementation currently throws from `setPermissionsEnabled`, so it needs an explicit V2 cleanup implementation (or equivalent listener handling) rather than suppressing the event.
